messages:
Sara Li: Quick sync — we need to settle reranker response semantics before the console rollout. Current ambiguity is hurting telemetry and cost math.
Maria Gomez: Agreed. Two recurring problems: 1) some models return "raw logits" and others normalized probs, 2) clients assume range [0,1]. We should pick a contract.
Alex Chen: +1. Also we need a way to represent tie-breaker / confidence so downstream can decide deterministic ordering.
Jon Patel: From product POV, exposing a simple probability is best for customers. But we still need raw values for debug/quality.
Priya Kapoor: Operationally we must cap candidates per request (we're seeing big O(length^2) KV cache blowups). What's the current safe cap?
Maria Gomez: Empirically 200 candidates is hurting latency at 512 token contexts. I propose default candidate_cap=64 and allow customers to opt into higher tiers (Dedicated).
Sara Li: Proposal sketch for API contract: always include two fields: "score" and "raw_score" (raw_score optional). Add explicit "score_type" enum: ["probability","logit","unnormalized"]. And a top-level "score_unit": "[0-1]" or "logit".
Alex Chen: Example envelope:
```
{
  "query": "...",
  "candidates": ["A","B","C"],
  "results": [
    {"candidate_id": 1, "score": 0.72, "raw_score": 2.03, "score_type": "probability"},
    {"candidate_id": 2, "score": 0.19, "raw_score": -1.44, "score_type": "probability"}
  ],
  "model": "rerank-small:v3",
  "score_unit": "[0-1]"
}
```
Sara Li: We should also support a "score_precision" int (e.g., 4) for controlling telemetry cardinality.
Maria Gomez: Important: define deterministic tie-breaking. Add "tie_breaker": "stable_index" or allow returning a small tie_noise value.
Jon Patel: Can we add a "top_k_exhaustive" flag for clients that want guarantees vs approximate top-k? That helps UX for relevance-sensitive features.
Priya Kapoor: For quotas: enforce both candidate_cap and tokens_per_rerank. Tokens accounting = query_tokens + sum(candidate_tokens). Prevent huge downstream token bills.
Alex Chen: Telemetry-wise, we need per-request fields shipped: model_version, candidate_count, top_k, average_score, score_type, fallback_used (bool), latency_ms, backend_queue_ms. Console needs to graph fallback rate/time series.
Maria Gomez: Also log summary histograms for score distributions (buckets) to detect drift/regressions. Keep bucket count small (e.g., 20) to avoid metric cardinality explosion.
Sara Li: Rollout UX: in console show per-model rollout % for rerankers, and a small compare view: A vs B on same traffic slice with precision@k and latency delta. Add automatic fallback policy: if latency or error rate exceeds threshold, route to a cheaper compatible variant.
Jon Patel: For the compare view, surface a human-readable note: "A yields 2% higher prec@10 but 40ms slower" — helpful for product owners.
Priya Kapoor: Ops: require a preset affinity map: route rule -> preferred rerank model, fallback chain, and max_candidates. So policy is explicit and auditable.
Alex Chen: Also add API param "model_affinity": ["rerank-large:v2","rerank-small:v3"] to let customer prefer in order. Platform should honor unless overloaded.
Maria Gomez: One more: eval-bot should add a synthetic test that hits the reranker with worst-case candidate count every deploy. eval-bot: running canary now.
eval-bot: starting reranker worst-case test on canary cluster (candidates=128, tokens=256 each).
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for rerank-small:v3 -> 5% traffic.
Sara Li: Next steps: 1) agree on JSON envelope (Sara will PR), 2) add telemetry fields and histograms (Maria + Alex), 3) console rollout UX mock (Jon), 4) update quota enforcement and docs (Priya).
Alex Chen: I'll draft the PR with the envelope and sample client code for JS/Go.
Jon Patel: I'll make the console mock by EOD Monday.
Maria Gomez: I'll add histogram buckets and a short note about score_type in the ML infra runbook.
Priya Kapoor: I'll add quota checks to the gateway: reject above candidate_cap or tokens_per_rerank with clear error code: 429 RERANK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
Sara Li: Awesome — thanks team. If nobody objects I'll open the RFC tonight. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: No objections from me.
Maria Gomez: SGTM.
Jon Patel: SGTM.
Priya Kapoor: SGTM.
Sara Li: Filing RFC: https://go/internal/rfcs/1790123456 (draft).
